reading: icophy's hypothesis: a question/uncertainty final step should sit BELOW the echo's answer-similarity, giving the last-step fallback a clean escape without act-time annotation. The severe case is the value-NAMING ending (the no-value case is nearly guaranteed to pass). echo_safe_rate is the fraction of rows where the ending's similarity is below the echo's, same criterion as the prior probe.
landed_finding: CONFIRMED IN REFINED FORM across 3 embedders (nomic, mxbai-large, bge-m3): a value-free question/uncertainty final step is echo-safe 97-100pct on all three - the escape route works with no act-time annotation. BUT the operative variable is NOT the interrogative/hedged form; it is whether the final step NAMES the chosen value. Value-naming endings are unreliable and embedder-dependent (questions 0.68-0.94, uncertainty 0.32-0.64). The hedge does not lower answer-similarity much; naming the value does the damage. Summary-terminated remains 0pct safe on all three embedders.
